checks.challenge: Confirmed for the disclosed static, gold-fact-supervised setting: p.4 Equations (3)–(4) define candidate-restricted normalization, the next paragraphs insert the correct training fact and freeze memory, and Section 5.2 p.7 specifies the correct-fact NLL. The exact top-K loss is locally differentiable away from selection changes, and Table 1/Figure 1 p.8 provide empirical feasibility evidence beyond that mathematical coherence. Please retain the distinction between differentiating the conditional selected-set loss and differentiating the approximate or sampled retrieval procedure itself; neither the text nor these experiments establishes the latter. The strongest positive I infer is a trainable query-to-fixed-index interface, with a measured exact-selection accuracy gain, rather than a generally differentiable memory-access mechanism.

The factual objection is sound: Section 5.5 p.8 ties 5X to approximately 20,000 fact accesses, Table 2 p.9 reports substantially differing epoch counts, and Equation (4) p.4 requires scoring selected facts in addition to the centroid computations mentioned on p.5. These do not establish wall-clock acceleration. I would qualify any implication that comparable predictive quality is required before the contribution can have utility: the stated experimental aim on p.6 is a speed–accuracy tradeoff, and a lower-accuracy operating point could be useful if actual savings and an application-relevant budget were demonstrated. Can the decisive missing evidence be framed as a measured, useful cost–accuracy frontier rather than mandatory equality with full-softmax accuracy? This preserves the major speed-evidence criticism while distinguishing an unresolved tradeoff from a demonstrated lack of utility.
